name: Marshal's Keep

stars.name: Keep Star
stars.notes: Old, steady G-dwarf slightly cooler than Sol. Its long-term stability has supported centuries of military logistics infrastructure without stellar interference.

planets.name: Anvil
planets.notes: Dense, metal-rich innermost world too hot for habitation. Automated mining platforms extract iron-group elements for the system's manufacturing base.

planets.name: Stockade
planets.notes: Primary depot world with breathable atmosphere. Population 22 million, mostly logistics corps and civilian contractors. Vast surface warehouses and underground storage vaults hold materiel for the rimward fleets.

planets.name: Fallow
planets.notes: Dry, cold world with thin carbon dioxide atmosphere. Agricultural domes dot the surface, growing supplemental food stocks for the depot's population and passing fleet elements.

planets.name: Bulkhead
planets.notes: Standard hydrogen-helium gas giant. Fuel-skimming operations on the upper atmosphere supply the depot's massive fuel reserves. Moon Tankard houses the primary fuel processing facility.

planets.name: Waypoint
planets.notes: Frozen outer world serving as a navigational reference and emergency supply cache. Subsurface water extraction supplements the system's consumables supply chain.

asteroid_belts.name: The Scrapyard
asteroid_belts.notes: A belt rich in processable metals, supplemented by decommissioned military hardware awaiting recycling. The line between natural asteroid and junked warship hull is sometimes blurry.

stations.name: Depot Meridian
stations.notes: Orbital logistics hub managing the inflow and outflow of military supplies. Handles an average of 200 supply ship arrivals per standard week. Massive automated cargo handling systems.

stations.name: Refueling Station Bravo
stations.notes: Fleet refueling station processing fuel skimmed from Bulkhead's atmosphere. Can simultaneously refuel eight capital ships.

stations.name: Repair Dock Seven
stations.notes: Intermediate repair facility handling battle damage and routine maintenance for warships operating in the rimward sectors. Four repair bays, limited to cruiser-class and below.

faction_control.notes: Rear-echelon military installation under Logistics Command jurisdiction. Security is moderate by military standards—the system's importance lies in supply rather than combat, though a permanent escort squadron is stationed here.

history: Established in 2411 as a forward supply depot to support Terran expansion into the rimward sectors, Marshal's Keep was named after Fleet Marshal Elara Vasquez, who identified the need for a dedicated logistics hub between the core worlds and the frontier.

During the Kethrani Wars, the system's supply throughput increased tenfold, and the depot's ability to sustain combat operations over extended campaigns was credited as a decisive factor in Terran victory by multiple post-war analyses.

In 2678, a Kethrani commando raid targeted Depot Meridian's automated cargo systems, introducing a logistics virus that corrupted supply manifests across the sector for three weeks before being detected and purged. The incident led to a comprehensive overhaul of supply chain security protocols.
description: Marshal's Keep is not a glamorous system. There are no imposing fortresses, no bristling weapons platforms, no dramatic gravitational anomalies. What there is, in quantities that would stagger a civilian accountant, is stuff. Five worlds orbit a quiet yellow star, and the system's purpose is to receive, store, process, and distribute the staggering volume of materiel required to sustain military operations across a dozen sectors. Stockade's surface is covered with warehouses. Its orbit is thick with cargo platforms. Supply ships arrive and depart in a constant stream that has not stopped in over two centuries.

The military significance of Marshal's Keep is of the unglamorous but essential variety. Warships do not fight without fuel, ammunition, spare parts, food, and medical supplies, and all of these flow through this system. Depot Meridian processes more cargo tonnage per week than most civilian spaceports handle in a year. Refueling Station Bravo around Bulkhead keeps the fleet mobile. Repair Dock Seven patches up damaged warships and returns them to service. The system is the logistical spine of Terran military operations in the rimward sectors, and its loss would cripple offensive capability within months.

The Kethrani clearly understand Marshal's Keep's importance, as the 2678 logistics virus attack demonstrated. The incident exposed a troubling vulnerability: the system's defenses are oriented toward repelling fleet-scale attacks, but it proved far less resilient against a surgical covert operation that targeted software rather than hardware. The Logistics Command has invested heavily in cybersecurity since, but officers privately acknowledge that a supply depot's openness to constant traffic makes it inherently more vulnerable to infiltration than a sealed military fortress. The next attack, they fear, may not target the computers but the supplies themselves.
